eg: Some parents believe a school uniform reduces pressure on children to wear expensive clothes.
egCn: 一些家长认为校服能减轻孩子穿昂贵衣服的压力。

eg: Studying abroad allows young people to become more independent and confident.
egCn: 出国留学能让年轻人变得更独立、更自信。

eg: Schools should teach life skills such as cooking, budgeting and managing time.
egCn: 学校应该教授烹饪、理财和时间管理等生活技能。

eg: Parents play an important role in educating their children about money.
egCn: 父母在教育孩子如何对待金钱方面发挥着重要作用。

eg: Science lessons are more memorable when students get hands-on experience in the laboratory.
egCn: 当学生在实验室里亲手操作时，科学课会让人印象更深刻。

eg: Gifted children may become bored if lessons move too slowly for them.
egCn: 如果课程进度对天资聪颖的孩子来说太慢，他们可能会感到厌倦。

eg: A good education should equip young people with the skills they need for work.
egCn: 良好的教育应当让年轻人具备工作所需的技能。

eg: Girls in some rural areas still have limited access to education.
egCn: 一些农村地区的女孩受教育的机会仍然有限。

eg: Online courses require a great deal of self-discipline because nobody checks your progress.
egCn: 网课需要很强的自律，因为没有人检查你的进度。

eg: Small classes create a more supportive learning environment for shy students.
egCn: 小班制能为内向的学生营造更有支持性的学习环境。

eg: Intense academic pressure can leave teenagers with little time for sleep or hobbies.
egCn: 繁重的学业压力会让青少年几乎没有时间睡觉或培养爱好。

eg: Spending a year abroad can broaden your horizons in ways no classroom can.
egCn: 在国外待一年能以课堂无法做到的方式开阔你的眼界。

cn: 逐步灌输；培养（观念、习惯）
eg: Team sports can instil discipline and a sense of fair play in young people.
egCn: 团体运动能逐步培养年轻人的纪律性和公平竞争意识。

eg: Teachers should nurture creativity rather than simply prepare students for exams.
egCn: 教师应该培养学生的创造力，而不是一味地让他们备考。

cn: 量身定制；使适合（特定需求）
eg: Online platforms can tailor lessons to the needs of each individual learner.
egCn: 在线平台可以根据每个学习者的需求量身定制课程。

cn: 应试的；以考试为导向的
eg: An exam-oriented system often rewards memory more than genuine understanding.
egCn: 应试体制往往更看重记忆力，而非真正的理解。

eg: In a student-centred classroom, learners discuss ideas instead of just listening to the teacher.
egCn: 在以学生为中心的课堂上，学习者会讨论观点，而不只是听老师讲。

cn: 全面发展的；多才多艺的
eg: Universities increasingly look for well-rounded applicants with interests beyond their studies.
egCn: 大学越来越青睐在学业之外也有兴趣爱好、全面发展的申请者。

eg: When school rankings depend on results, teachers are tempted to teach to the test.
egCn: 当学校排名取决于考试成绩时，老师就容易为了考试而教学。
collocations: be forced to teach to the test

eg: Research shows a strong link between family income and educational attainment.
egCn: 研究表明，家庭收入与受教育程度之间存在密切联系。

eg: Long working hours leave many parents with little time to spend with their children.
egCn: 长时间工作让许多父母几乎没有时间陪伴孩子。

eg: Many graduates choose well-paid jobs in finance instead of careers they truly enjoy.
egCn: 许多毕业生选择金融业的高薪工作，而不是自己真正喜欢的职业。

eg: Since the pandemic, many office staff have been allowed to work from home twice a week.
egCn: 疫情以来，许多办公室职员获准每周在家办公两天。
collocations: the right to work from home

eg: Graduates now face a highly competitive job market, especially in creative industries.
egCn: 如今毕业生面临竞争非常激烈的就业市场，在创意产业尤其如此。

cn: 职业道路；职业发展路径
eg: Few people today follow a single career path from graduation until retirement.
egCn: 如今很少有人从毕业到退休一直走同一条职业道路。

eg: Employees who feel pressured to avoid sick leave often spread illness around the office.
egCn: 迫于压力不敢请病假的员工常常把疾病传染给办公室里的其他人。

cn: 承担（工作、责任）；接受；雇用
eg: Young employees are often keen to take on extra responsibility to prove themselves.
egCn: 年轻员工往往乐于承担额外的责任来证明自己。

eg: Robots are increasingly used for repetitive tasks on factory production lines.
egCn: 机器人越来越多地被用来完成工厂生产线上的重复性工作。

cn: 有意义的；值得做的；有回报的
eg: Nursing is exhausting, but many nurses describe it as an extremely rewarding job.
egCn: 护理工作很累人，但许多护士形容它是一份非常有意义的工作。

eg: Women and men doing the same job should receive equal pay by law.
egCn: 按照法律，从事相同工作的女性和男性应获得同等报酬。

eg: Several countries have raised the retirement age because people are living longer.
egCn: 由于人们寿命延长，一些国家已提高了退休年龄。

cn: 职业；（需专业训练的）行业；同业人员
eg: Teaching is a demanding profession that deserves greater respect and better pay.
egCn: 教书是一项要求很高的职业，理应得到更多尊重和更好的薪酬。

cn: 令人满足的；有成就感的
eg: For many people, a fulfilling job matters more than a high salary.
egCn: 对许多人来说，一份有成就感的工作比高薪更重要。

eg: Assembly line work can be so monotonous that staff lose concentration and make mistakes.
egCn: 流水线工作可能单调到让员工注意力涣散、频频出错。

eg: Many women find it harder to climb the career ladder after having children.
egCn: 许多女性发现生孩子之后在职场上晋升变得更难了。

eg: Working parents often struggle to strike a balance between their jobs and family life.
egCn: 上班的父母常常难以在工作与家庭生活之间取得平衡。

eg: Publishing salary data could help companies close the gender pay gap more quickly.
egCn: 公开薪资数据可以帮助企业更快地缩小性别薪酬差距。

eg: Internships can greatly improve the employability of students without work experience.
egCn: 实习可以大大提高缺乏工作经验的学生的就业能力。

cn: 不稳定的；不牢靠的；危险的
eg: Delivery riders often live in a precarious position, with no sick pay or pension.
egCn: 外卖骑手常常处境不稳定，既没有病假工资也没有养老金。

cn: 零工时合同（不保证最低工时的雇佣合同）
eg: Workers on zero-hours contracts never know how much they will earn each week.
egCn: 签零工时合同的工人永远不知道自己每周能挣多少钱。

eg: More police officers on the streets would make residents feel safer at night.
egCn: 街上有更多警察会让居民在夜间感到更安全。

eg: Prisoners who learn a trade are less likely to commit crimes after release.
egCn: 学会一门手艺的囚犯出狱后再犯罪的可能性更小。

eg: Some teenagers steal from shops for excitement rather than because they need the items.
egCn: 有些青少年在商店偷东西是为了寻求刺激，而不是因为需要那些物品。

eg: Offenders who serve a short sentence rarely receive any education or job training in prison.
egCn: 服短期徒刑的罪犯在狱中很少接受任何教育或职业培训。

eg: Keeping non-violent offenders behind bars costs taxpayers a huge amount of money.
egCn: 把非暴力罪犯关在牢里要花费纳税人大量的钱。

eg: Better street lighting has helped reduce petty crime such as bicycle theft.
egCn: 更好的街道照明有助于减少偷自行车之类的轻微犯罪。

eg: Some argue that harsh punishments do little to stop young people from offending.
egCn: 有人认为，严厉的惩罚对阻止年轻人犯罪作用不大。

eg: Politicians often promise to be tough on crime because it wins votes.
egCn: 政客们常常承诺严厉打击犯罪，因为这样能赢得选票。

eg: Young people with no hope of finding work may turn to crime.
egCn: 找不到工作、看不到希望的年轻人可能会走上犯罪道路。
collocations: turn to crime out of desperation
drive people to turn to crime

eg: He received a life sentence for murdering two people during a robbery.
egCn: 他因在抢劫中杀害两人而被判处无期徒刑。

eg: Criminal gangs smuggle drugs across borders hidden inside ordinary goods.
egCn: 犯罪团伙把毒品藏在普通货物中走私过境。

eg: A well-funded police force can respond to emergencies much more quickly.
egCn: 资金充足的警队能够更快地响应紧急情况。

eg: Visible security cameras may deter thieves from targeting a particular street.
egCn: 醒目的监控摄像头可能会让小偷不敢对某条街道下手。

eg: Education in prison helps former offenders reintegrate into society after release.
egCn: 狱中教育有助于刑满释放人员出狱后重新融入社会。

eg: International cooperation is essential to fight drug trafficking and people smuggling.
egCn: 打击毒品贩运和人口偷渡离不开国际合作。

eg: Overcrowded prisons make it difficult for staff to keep inmates safe.
egCn: 监狱人满为患，让工作人员难以保障在押人员的安全。

eg: Fewer than half of those arrested for fraud are eventually convicted.
egCn: 因诈骗被捕的人中，最终被定罪的不到一半。

eg: White-collar crime such as tax fraud often receives lighter punishment than street crime.
egCn: 逃税之类的白领犯罪受到的惩罚往往比街头犯罪轻。

eg: A stronger police presence in city centres can discourage violence on weekend nights.
egCn: 加强市中心的警力部署可以减少周末夜晚的暴力事件。

eg: A purely punitive approach ignores the social causes that lead people into crime.
egCn: 单纯的惩罚性做法忽视了导致人们犯罪的社会根源。

eg: Reality TV often rewards bad behaviour because arguments attract more viewers.
egCn: 真人秀节目往往助长不良行为，因为争吵能吸引更多观众。

eg: Influencers with millions of followers can shape what young people buy and wear.
egCn: 拥有数百万粉丝的网红能左右年轻人的消费和穿着。

eg: A shocking news story can spread around the world within a few minutes.
egCn: 一条令人震惊的新闻几分钟内就能传遍全世界。

eg: Television campaigns have helped raise awareness of the dangers of drink-driving.
egCn: 电视宣传活动帮助提高了人们对酒驾危害的认识。

eg: False rumours about vaccines spread quickly through social media groups.
egCn: 关于疫苗的虚假谣言在社交媒体群组中迅速传播。

eg: Small restaurants rely mainly on word of mouth rather than expensive advertising.
egCn: 小餐馆主要靠口碑，而不是昂贵的广告。

cn: 有说服力的；令人信服的
eg: Advertisements aimed at children use persuasive techniques that young minds cannot easily resist.
egCn: 针对儿童的广告运用了极具说服力的手法，孩子们很难抵挡。

eg: Companies spend huge sums on marketing to make their products seem essential.
egCn: 企业在营销上投入巨资，让自己的产品显得不可或缺。

eg: Scientific research should be explained in language the general public can understand.
egCn: 科学研究应该用普通大众能理解的语言来解释。

eg: Many teenagers now dream of becoming content creators rather than doctors or lawyers.
egCn: 如今许多青少年梦想成为内容创作者，而不是医生或律师。

eg: Students need to learn how to tell whether a website is trustworthy.
egCn: 学生需要学会判断一个网站是否可信。

eg: Celebrities who are constantly in the spotlight have almost no private life.
egCn: 总处在聚光灯下的名人几乎没有私生活。

eg: Journalists should fact-check every claim before publishing a story online.
egCn: 记者在网上发布报道之前应该核查每一项说法。

eg: Edited photos and videos can be used to manipulate public opinion during elections.
egCn: 经过剪辑的照片和视频可能在选举期间被用来操纵舆论。

eg: Reading several news outlets helps people avoid relying on a single point of view.
egCn: 阅读多家新闻媒体的报道有助于人们避免只依赖单一观点。

eg: Many readers find intrusive photos of grieving families deeply disrespectful.
egCn: 许多读者认为，拍摄悲痛家属的侵扰性照片极不尊重人。

cn: （以信息、问题等）狂轰滥炸；轰炸
eg: Children are bombarded with advertisements for snacks every time they watch videos online.
egCn: 孩子们每次在网上看视频都会被零食广告狂轰滥炸。

eg: The newspaper refused to reveal the name of the whistle-blower who exposed the safety failures.
egCn: 这家报纸拒绝透露揭发安全问题的举报人的姓名。

eg: Some teachers believe short videos are shortening students' attention spans.
egCn: 一些老师认为短视频正在缩短学生的注意力持续时间。

eg: Paid advertisements on social media may sway undecided voters in close elections.
egCn: 社交媒体上的付费广告可能会在势均力敌的选举中左右尚未拿定主意的选民。

eg: The government should provide free childcare so that more parents can return to work.
egCn: 政府应该提供免费托儿服务，让更多父母能够重返工作岗位。

eg: In many countries, museums are open to visitors free of charge.
egCn: 在许多国家，博物馆向游客免费开放。

eg: Public transport should be free for the elderly so that they can stay active.
egCn: 公共交通应该对老年人免费，这样他们才能保持活跃。

eg: Governments need to regulate social media companies more strictly to protect children.
egCn: 各国政府需要更严格地监管社交媒体公司以保护儿童。

eg: Critics say public funds should not be spent on building new football stadiums.
egCn: 批评者认为不应该用公共资金修建新的足球场。

eg: Newspapers may publish private information only when it is clearly in the public interest.
egCn: 报纸只有在明显符合公共利益时才可以公开私人信息。

eg: If governments do not take action now, traffic in big cities will only get worse.
egCn: 如果政府现在不采取行动，大城市的交通只会越来越糟。

eg: The government plans to phase out new petrol cars over the next ten years.
egCn: 政府计划在未来十年内逐步淘汰新的汽油车。

eg: Raising taxes on cigarettes is an effective way to reduce smoking.
egCn: 提高香烟税是减少吸烟的有效办法。

eg: The council has set aside money to repair roads and build new cycle paths.
egCn: 市议会已拨出资金修路和修建新的自行车道。

eg: The party in power often changes policies just before an election to win support.
egCn: 执政党常常在选举前夕调整政策以赢得支持。

eg: Banning fireworks in residential areas would improve public safety during festivals.
egCn: 在居民区禁放烟花可以提升节日期间的公共安全。

eg: Ministers promised to clamp down on companies that avoid paying their fair share of tax.
egCn: 部长们承诺严厉打击那些逃避缴纳应缴税款的公司。

eg: New laws are useless unless the authorities have the resources to enforce them.
egCn: 如果当局没有资源去执行，新的法律就毫无用处。

eg: Some countries have made voting mandatory to increase participation in elections.
egCn: 一些国家已将投票定为强制义务，以提高选举参与度。

eg: Greater transparency about how tax money is spent would rebuild public trust.
egCn: 更公开透明地说明税款的去向，将有助于重建公众信任。

eg: Small businesses complain that too much red tape slows down their growth.
egCn: 小企业抱怨过多的繁文缛节拖慢了它们的发展。

eg: Mass surveillance may reduce crime, but it also threatens civil liberties.
egCn: 大规模监控也许能减少犯罪，但也威胁到公民自由。

cn: 保姆式国家（指管得过多的政府）
eg: Opponents call the sugar tax another example of the nanny state telling people what to eat.
egCn: 反对者称糖税是保姆式国家对人们吃什么指手画脚的又一例证。

eg: Why should taxpayers foot the bill for repairing damage caused by large companies?
egCn: 为什么要由纳税人为大公司造成的损害买单？
collocations: be left to foot the bill

eg: Tourism has changed the traditional way of life on many small islands.
egCn: 旅游业改变了许多小岛上的传统生活方式。

eg: Traditional festivals are often public holidays, so families can celebrate together.
egCn: 传统节日通常是公共假日，这样家人就可以一起庆祝。

eg: Learning a foreign language helps people understand how others see the world.
egCn: 学习外语有助于人们理解别人如何看待世界。

cn: 艺术（音乐、绘画、戏剧等的总称）
eg: Cutting government funding for the arts could force many small theatres to close.
egCn: 削减政府对艺术的资助可能会迫使许多小剧院关门。

eg: Many local dialects are dying out because young people only speak the national language.
egCn: 许多地方方言正在消亡，因为年轻人只说国家通用语言。
collocations: be in danger of dying out

eg: Children who move abroad can lose touch with their family's culture and language.
egCn: 移居国外的孩子可能会与自己家族的文化和语言渐渐疏远。

eg: Travelling abroad tends to make young people more open-minded about different customs.
egCn: 出国旅行往往让年轻人对不同习俗更加开明包容。

eg: Schools can promote tolerance by teaching children about other religions and traditions.
egCn: 学校可以通过向孩子们介绍其他宗教和传统来提倡宽容。

eg: Newcomers often change their accent or clothing in order to fit in.
egCn: 新来的人常常会改变口音或穿着以便融入当地。

eg: Student cultural exchange programmes help break down stereotypes between nations.
egCn: 学生文化交流项目有助于打破国家之间的刻板印象。

eg: American films and music still dominate popular culture in many parts of the world.
egCn: 美国电影和音乐仍然主导着世界许多地区的流行文化。

eg: My grandparents speak a local dialect that even people in the next town find hard to follow.
egCn: 我祖父母说的当地方言，连邻镇的人都很难听懂。

eg: The town revived its old harvest festival to attract tourists and bring residents together.
egCn: 该镇恢复了古老的丰收节，以吸引游客并凝聚居民。

eg: Mass tourism can damage a heritage site if visitor numbers are not carefully controlled.
egCn: 如果不严格控制游客数量，大规模旅游可能会破坏遗产地。

eg: Cities that embrace immigrants often benefit from new ideas, food and business.
egCn: 接纳移民的城市往往会受益于新的思想、美食和商业。

cn: 大熔炉（多种族、多文化融合之地）
eg: London has become a melting pot of languages, cuisines and religions.
egCn: 伦敦已成为多种语言、美食和宗教交融的大熔炉。

eg: Deep-rooted beliefs about gender roles are slow to change, even in wealthy countries.
egCn: 关于性别角色的根深蒂固的观念改变得很慢，即使在富裕国家也是如此。

eg: Meeting people from other backgrounds is one of the best ways to reduce prejudice.
egCn: 与不同背景的人接触是减少偏见的最好方法之一。

eg: Many people feel that traditional festivals have become too commercialised in recent years.
egCn: 许多人觉得传统节日近年来变得过于商业化了。

eg: Economic hardship can fuel xenophobia, as people blame foreigners for losing their jobs.
egCn: 经济困难可能助长排外情绪，因为人们把失业归咎于外国人。

eg: Charging customers for plastic bags has greatly reduced the number thrown away.
egCn: 向顾客收取塑料袋费用大大减少了被丢弃的塑料袋数量。

eg: Simple habits like switching off lights can save energy and lower household bills.
egCn: 随手关灯之类的简单习惯可以节约能源，降低家庭开支。

eg: Visitors to national parks should take their rubbish home with them.
egCn: 国家公园的游客应该把自己的垃圾带回家。

eg: Families can cut down on waste by buying only the food they need.
egCn: 家庭可以只买需要的食物来减少浪费。

eg: Many countries plan to switch to electric buses within the next ten years.
egCn: 许多国家计划在未来十年内改用电动公交车。

eg: Energy-efficient appliances cost more at first but save money over time.
egCn: 节能电器起初价格更高，但长期来看能省钱。

eg: Old coal power stations are being closed and replaced by wind and solar farms.
egCn: 老旧的燃煤电站正被关闭，取而代之的是风电场和太阳能电站。

eg: Extreme weather such as floods and heatwaves is becoming more frequent worldwide.
egCn: 洪水和热浪等极端天气在全球范围内越来越频繁。

eg: It is wasteful to heat empty offices when nobody is working there.
egCn: 在没人上班时给空荡荡的办公室供暖是一种浪费。

eg: Supermarkets could reduce food waste by giving unsold products to charities.
egCn: 超市可以把卖不掉的食品捐给慈善机构来减少食物浪费。

eg: More companies are going green because customers prefer environmentally responsible brands.
egCn: 越来越多的公司走上环保路线，因为顾客更青睐对环境负责的品牌。

eg: Rising ocean temperatures could wipe out large areas of coral reef.
egCn: 海洋温度上升可能会摧毁大片珊瑚礁。

eg: Heavy use of chemical fertilisers is detrimental to soil quality in the long term.
